definition: The two definitions are talking about the same thing. That does not mean the scales can be swapped.
label: Same concept

definition: Everything that counts as A also counts as B, but B covers other cases too. More than just a change of setting.
label: A is a type of B

definition: Everything that counts as B also counts as A, but A covers other cases too. More than just a change of setting.
label: B is a type of A

definition: A is mainly B limited to a domain, object, or task.
label: A is B in a particular setting

definition: B is mainly A limited to a domain, object, or task.
label: B is A in a particular setting

definition: A is a piece or dimension of B, not a subtype of B.
label: A is part of B

definition: B is a piece or dimension of A, not a subtype of A.
label: B is part of A

definition: Two distinct kinds under the same broader idea. Sharing a topic is not enough.
label: Parallel concepts

definition: They share some of what they mean, or some of the cases they cover, but each also goes beyond the other.
label: Partial overlap

definition: None of the types above fit, but there is still a link (for example, one leads to the other). A short note helps.
label: Other relationship

definition: The definitions are clear enough, but they do not support any of the links above. They may still be correlated.
label: None of the above

definition: More than one of the links above is reasonable, and picking a single one would be forced. List them in the note if you like.
label: More than one applies

definition: The materials are too thin or too unclear. You do not need to look anything else up.
label: Can't tell from the materials
